chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Hammad ibn Isa from Shu'ayb from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who had partnership capital (mal al-mudarabah), and he died while having a debt, and he bequeathed that which he left to the partners of the mudarabah. Is that permissible? He said: 'Yes, if it is verified/confirmed.'

key_terms.مَالُ مُضَارَبَةٍ: Partnership capital (investment capital in a mudarabah contract)
key_terms.مُصَدَّقاً: Verified or confirmed (referring to the existence and validity of the bequeathed asset)

ai.seo_question: Can a deceased person bequeath their partnership capital to the partners if they have outstanding debts?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the priority of a specific bequest (*wasiyya*) of *mudarabah* capital over general debts, ruling its validity contingent upon the capital's actual existence and verification (*tasdiq*). This highlights the Shia juristic principle that while debts generally take precedence, a verified bequest of partnership assets remains enforceable, reflecting the practical application of commercial law in inheritance. The condition of *tasdiq* ensures that the bequest is not merely nominal but represents real, available assets, preserving the rights of both creditors and partners.
